# Building a More Connected CTV Ecosystem with OpenRTB 2.6


Magnite Team


November 19, 2026 | 4 min read


As programmatic CTV matures, the industry is getting more sophisticated about how an ad break is represented, bought and sold. An ad break is not simply a collection of unrelated impressions: each opportunity has a position, duration and relationship to the others around it. OpenRTB 2.6 ad podding provides a standardized way for publishers, SSPs and DSPs to represent that structure in the transaction.


That gives buyers a clearer view of the inventory available across an entire break, including how individual opportunities fit together. For publishers, that context can create more opportunities for competitive bids while preserving control over how inventory is sold. For DSPs, podding can also improve efficiency by reducing queries per second (QPS) and associated infrastructure demands.


Magnite has been supporting publishers with high-quality ad break and playlist assembly for years. The growing adoption of OpenRTB 2.6 extends that work into a more standardized way of representing and transacting CTV ad breaks.


Magnite is expanding OpenRTB 2.6 to cover transactions with DSP partners including Google Display & Video 360, Amazon DSP, Yahoo DSP, Moloco, and others. Each integration has its own technical requirements, and Magnite is supporting those requirements as they evolve. Together with the discovery, implementation and measurement work undertaken by the DSPs, these efforts give publishers more ways to participate in standardized CTV transactions while minimizing disruption to how they manage and monetize their inventory.


**Why OpenRTB 2.6 Matters for CTV**


A CTV ad break can contain multiple ad opportunities, each with a defined position, duration and value. A three-slot break, for example, might include a 15-second opportunity followed by two 30-second slots. Historically, SSPs and DSPs have often represented those opportunities as separate bid requests, giving buyers limited visibility into how each fits within the overall break. Magnite has long supported[podded ad calling](https://www.magnite.com/blog/smarter-pods-better-breaks-the-future-of-ctv-monetization/) , bringing multiple opportunities within the same break to market together.


OpenRTB 2.6 ad podding provides a standardized way to represent the ad pod structure in the bid request. The specification can communicate the break’s position within the content stream, total duration available for dynamic ad insertion, number and position of opportunities, and eligible creative durations. It can also support duration-based pricing, helping buyers and sellers account for differences in value across creative lengths.


Standardizing that information improves transaction efficiency. Fewer redundant bid requests can reduce QPS, while clearer duration and position signals can reduce bids that cannot be used because of creative-length conflicts or pod constraints. At ad assembly, that can mean fewer unfilled slots, less unused inventory and less risk of dead air.


The result is a bid request that carries more of the information needed to transact on a CTV ad break as a structured unit—giving DSPs greater visibility while giving publishers a consistent way to represent their inventory across demand partners.


**Supporting Both Sides of the Transaction as Standards Evolve**


Adopting OpenRTB 2.6 is not a one-size-fits-all process. DSP implementations can vary in their technical requirements, and publishers need to understand how those requirements affect their existing ad-serving, yield-management and monetization workflows.


Magnite is supporting publishers through that transition[with implementation guidance](https://www.magnite.com/blog/beyond-roas-why-incremental-lifetime-value-is-ctvs-next-frontier/) , FAQs, training and technical support across OpenRTB 2.6 workflows and partner-specific requirements. The goal is to make it easier for publishers to adopt new standards without having to redesign their existing CTV infrastructure for each demand partner.


For buyers, broader adoption of OpenRTB 2.6 makes it easier to evaluate CTV inventory across supply partners. Grouping multiple opportunities from the same ad break into one request also helps DSPs reduce QPS and respond with bids that better match the available positions and creative lengths.


That flexibility is important[as the CTV ecosystem](https://www.magnite.com/blog/bridging-the-gap-between-data-and-supply-inside-clearlines-self-serve-audience-capabilities/) continues to evolve. Publishers should be able to connect their inventory to the demand partners and platforms that make sense for their businesses while maintaining control over how their inventory is packaged, offered and monetized.


By building OpenRTB 2.6 support across multiple DSP integrations—and supporting the specific requirements of each implementation—Magnite is helping publishers participate in more standardized CTV transactions while retaining control over their supply and monetization strategy.
